summary.text: A 56-year-old nulligravida woman presented with abnormal uterine bleeding after cervical cytology showed atypical glandular cells and a cervical biopsy raised suspicion of adenocarcinoma. Endometrial biopsy confirmed clear cell carcinoma. Pelvic MRI suggested invasion of more than half of the myometrium with the lesion localized to the uterus, and neck, chest and pelvis CT showed no distant metastasis or lymphadenopathy.

She underwent total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral adnexectomy, partial omentectomy, appendectomy and pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy. Postoperative pathology identified clear cell carcinoma with myometrial invasion of 8/18 mm and cervical stromal invasion, without vascular invasion or lymph node metastasis, giving stage II (FIGO 2008). Six courses of carboplatin and paclitaxel every 3 weeks were given, with CT showing no recurrence, followed by observation.

Approximately 2 months after completing chemotherapy she developed gradually progressive trismus and left mandibular pain, was diagnosed with temporomandibular joint disorder at a local dental clinic and did not improve. CT of the jaw 5 months after chemotherapy showed a left mandibular mass; she revisited the hospital, CT showed a 4 cm mass with bone destruction and PET-CT showed uptake. Needle biopsy and immunohistochemistry were consistent with recurrence of clear cell carcinoma, pMMR.

Surgery and radiation therapy were considered, but chemotherapy with lenvatinib and pembrolizumab was chosen and started. Trismus and pain improved for four weeks; grade 2 uveitis, fatigue and grade 2 rash occurred. Lenvatinib was stopped after the third pembrolizumab course, CT showed shrinkage and then no detectable lesion after the sixth cycle, a complete response by RECIST maintained, with no recurrence for over a year.
